newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-FRANCE'S MOST CAPPED PLAYER FORCED TO RETIRE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FRANCE'S MOST CAPPED PLAYER FORCED TO RETIRE.

text.p: Manuel Amoros, France's most capped player, has been forced to quit soccer because of acute arthritis at the age of 34.
Amoros, who played in two World Cup semifinals in 1982 and 1986 and helped Michel Platini's side win the 1984 European championship, won 82 caps in 10 years as an international.
Once regarded as the world's finest right back, Amoros gradually faded out of the game quietly after winning a fourth French league title with Marseille and sixth overall in 1993.
"I naturally provided support to the attackers. It was in my temperament," said Amoros, who always wore the number two France jersey.
"I recall rival forwards saying `stop going up, all we can do with you is defend' he said in Thursday's sports daily L'Equipe.
The quiet and shy Amoros is proud of his achievements and, although not bitter, is unhappy they are not recognised more.

"I'm not Canto (Eric Cantona), each has his character. But I deplore the fact there isn't more recognition of my record," said Amoros, who believes he has plenty to offer his country as it prepares to host the 1998 World Cup finals.
"I've played in two World Cups, I could help with the organisation of a venue like Marseille."
Amoros began his career at Monaco, with whom he made his first division debut at 18.
The month before his 20th birthday in January 1982, he made his France debut under coach Michel Hidalgo in a 2-0 win over Italy.
After two league titles and one French Cup win with Monaco, Amoros moved to Marseille in 1989.

He helped Marseille win four championships in a row, although they were subsequently stripped of the 1993 title, and reach the 1991 European Cup final in Bari where he missed a penalty in the decisive shootout against Red Star Belgrade.
Amoros was no longer first choice when Marseille won the European Cup in May 1993.
He played 461 league matches and scored 41 goals, ending his first division career with Lyon between 1993 and 1995.
He returned to Marseille, who were in the second division, but only managed 16 matches in their 1995/96 promotion season.

He was forced through his arthritis of the hip to turn down an offer three months ago from Puebla of Mexico, the place where he scored his only international goal, a penalty, to help France win the 1986 World Cup third place playoff against Belgium.
The condition appears to be hereditary. Amoros' father underwent surgery on an arthritic right hip four years ago and he may need the same operation.
Amoros ended his France career at the European championship finals in Sweden in 1992. His last match was the 2-1 defeat by Denmark, who went on to win the trophy.
He said he would show his baby son the videos of his two World Cup semifinal appearances.
"Then he'll know his daddy was not long ago one of the best full backs in the world."
